title: Stack Sortable Permutation
description:
You are given an integer array `perm` representing a permutation of `1, 2, ..., n` arriving on an input track from left to right. You have a single LIFO siding stack. At each step you may either push the next element of `perm` onto the stack or pop the top element of the stack onto the output track.

Return `true` if it is possible to emit `[1, 2, ..., n]` in strictly ascending order on the output track, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: perm is a permutation of integers from 1 to perm.length.
hints: Maintain the next expected output integer `need` (starting at 1) alongside a simulation stack.
Push each element of `perm` onto the stack and immediately pop while the stack top equals `need`, incrementing `need`; the permutation is stack-sortable iff `need` reaches `n + 1`.

examples.explanation: Push 3, push 2, push 1, then pop 1, 2, 3 to produce [1, 2, 3].
2 must stay on the stack while waiting for 1, which traps 3 above 2 after 1 is popped, making [1, 2, 3] impossible.
Push 2, push 1, pop 1, pop 2, push 4, push 3, pop 3, pop 4 produces [1, 2, 3, 4].
